rubric_verdicts.rationale: Assessed from source across the capture cells, not from pixels: a collection row's identity link goes to the scoped detail route, the detail page leads with the action band whose buttons open the review drawer, the step-up form submits to one handler, and the result renders as a status region with a scoped activity link, so no dead end or unlabelled step was found on the list, detail, action, result path. Rendered keyboard order and focus return are measured by the UXQ-02 mounted journey, not by this record.

findings.claim: The subscription detail page overrides its normal group rhythm with page-tier gaps of 1px, 3px and 0 (and a raw 0 0.25rem field gap), so the summary, facts, resources and disclosure groups read as one compressed block instead of the title, lifecycle, facts hierarchy the contract specifies.
findings.rationale: D-34: delete the page-tier overrides so the component tokens apply and replace the raw field gap with --ax-space-xs. The page tier is the lowest tier that owns these selectors. The mechanical check scanSubscriptionDetailSpacing finds them at source_commit and must find none at fix_commit.

findings.claim: The Phase 253 audit reported the collection heading at 24px against a 28px page-heading contract. The shared display rule is already responsive (1.5rem, 24px, below 768px; 1.75rem, 28px, from 768px), so the contract row, not the rule, is wrong; the two rem literals can move to --ax-type-xl and --ax-type-2xl with no visual change.
findings.rationale: D-34: amend the contract to a responsive heading and leave shared .ax-display semantics untouched. The heading red test is DR-254-02:source (the declared literals); DR-254-02:computed at 767 and 768 CSS px passes before and after by design.

contract.amended_text: | Page heading | Responsive: `--ax-type-xl` (24px) below 768px, `--ax-type-2xl` (28px) from 768px | Semibold 600 | 1.2 |
contract.note: 254-12 performs the edit and keeps the section's introductory sentence consistent with its rows.

findings.claim: Detail field labels resolve to 14px semibold uppercase (the bare .ax-field-label rule) while the contract label role is 12px semibold, so detail labels are larger than the summary keys they sit beside.
findings.rationale: D-34: scope a font: var(--ax-type-label-sm-font) rule to .ax-field-list .ax-field-label so detail labels equal summary keys at --ax-type-xs. The bare .ax-field-label stays untouched (six form controls share it) and .ax-field-value keeps tabular-nums.

findings.claim: Detail disclosure headings render at 20px (--ax-type-lg), which is outside the contract's declared size steps, although the brandbook's seven-step type scale in theme.css defines 20px as the title role.
findings.rationale: D-34: the brandbook scale is authoritative, so the contract gains a Section title role; no CSS changes. The identical duplicate selector is a separate deferral (DR-254-09).

contract.note: 254-12 performs the edit and keeps the section's introductory sentence consistent with its rows.

findings.claim: The action-result link label and its scoped events path exist twice: SubscriptionLive owns the literal and the path builder privately, and the Storybook page scenario adapter repeats both, so the static result story can drift from the mounted page.
findings.rationale: D-34: add Copy.subscription_action_activity_link_label/0 and a public @doc false SubscriptionLive.action_activity_path/3, and have the LiveView and the story adapter call both, as the adapter already does for action_result_message/1. The result link appears after a dispatch, which none of the 16 captures reach, so the proof is an ExUnit owner test plus a literal-count guard.

findings.claim: The Activity audit log heading is the only section title at font-weight 950 and the only one coloured with --ax-accent-readable. The Phase 253 contract allows two weights and reserves the accent for the eligible action, the selected view, text links and focus; 950 is a third weight and the accent here marks a heading.
findings.rationale: Whether the audit ledger heading should carry deliberate emphasis is a product and brand judgment the plan does not settle, it cannot be decided by a mechanical check, and the rule is already tagged for the type-system pass. D-36 defers anything that is not one of the five locked dispositions.
findings.verdict_reason: deferred by D-36: no correction was made, so there is nothing to confirm; the condition remains and is tracked as DEF-254-04

findings.claim: The audit strip is captioned "Audit event table: Actor / Action / Timestamp", which describes a table structure in implementer language, while the element below it is a three-item summary row labelled "Latest audit event summary" and no table.

findings.claim: The subscription detail disclosures use <summary class="ax-detail-section-head">, a flex row with a 22px minimum height, and do not use .ax-disclosure-summary, which gives the webhook detail disclosures a 44px target, a pointer cursor, a chevron and an explicit focus ring. Whether the default marker and focus ring render acceptably is a runtime question; this record asserts only the class difference.
findings.rationale: Target size and keyboard focus are measured by the UXQ-02 probes (254-11): if they route a defect on summary.ax-detail-section-head it is fixed in the correction batch as a routed accessibility defect; otherwise sharing .ax-disclosure-summary across detail views is a design decision that reaches several LiveViews and is deferred (D-36). 254-13 re-disposition: none of the 30 routed accessibility entries (register at eefee2a62958dbdefe426d5434ed133e91b3e8ec) names summary.ax-detail-section-head (A11Y-254-22 names summary.ax-button, the menu button), and the 151 composition cells now report 0 observations, so no defect was routed and the finding stays deferred (D-36).
findings.verdict_reason: deferred by D-36: no correction was made, so there is nothing to confirm; the condition remains and is tracked as DEF-254-06

amendments.rationale: The Phase 253 collection universe has no populated state: the compiled collection states are new_host_empty, filtered_empty, queue_empty, one_row, multiple_rows, page_boundary, loading, unavailable, partial_cursor_error and incomplete_projection. multiple_rows is the populated collection.

amendments.original: D-35 shows every correction red on the pre-fix commit, which for the heading amendment would be a computed assertion at 767 and 768 CSS px
amendments.amended: The heading amendment's red is carried by DR-254-02:source (the declared font-size literals 1.5rem and 1.75rem against var(--ax-type-xl) and var(--ax-type-2xl)); DR-254-02:computed at 767 and 768 CSS px passes before and after by design
amendments.rationale: The shared .ax-display rule was already responsive (24px below 768px, 28px from 768px), so the contract row was wrong and the rendered heading does not change; a computed assertion cannot be red for a contract-only amendment, while the token literals are a real source change that can.

amendments.original: Design corrections are confined to the 16 D-33 capture cells (D-36)
amendments.amended: Routed accessibility defects are fixed wherever 254-11 observed them (D-08 W4): 10 routed cells fall inside the 16 captures and 102 composition cells fall outside them, and all are fixed in this batch with their register entries deleted
amendments.rationale: An accessibility defect is fixed at the lowest tier that owns it, not only on the cells that happen to be captured; the cells outside the 16 are listed here so the wider reach is a recorded, owner-accepted decision rather than silent scope growth.
